newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Trade seen topping Centam agenda for Clinton visit.
newsitem.headline: Trade seen topping Centam agenda for Clinton visit.

text.p: Trade will be among the top items when Central American leaders meet with U.S. President Bill Clinton in Costa Rica in May, officials said on Friday.

"Clearly one of the themes is trade, or more exactly, the concern that Central America has that we lost a competitive advantage because of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA)," Guatemalan Foreign Relations Minister Eduardo Stein said.
He was one of a group of Central American foreign ministers and ambassadors to the United States who met in Guatemala on Friday to plan a joint strategy on trade and other issues.

Officials said they would either seek parity with NAFTA -- trade with the United States and Canada on terms similar to that which Mexico enjoys under NAFTA. Or they would seek wider preferences for Central American products, especially textiles and shoes, under the Caribbean Basin Initiative (CBI).

Prior to the meeting, positions of the different countries on what to seek from Clinton appeared to range all over the map. Guatemala supported direct free trade negotiations between Central America and the NAFTA countries.
Nicaraguan Foreign Minister Emilio Alvarez said Nicaragua was interested in asking for NAFTA parity.
His Costa Rican couterpart Fernando Naranjo said NAFTA parity was too small a goal because the United States was not the only market for Central American products.

The region should be positioning itself to become part of a larger Latin American free trade group and meanwhile could seek modifications to benefits in the U.S. market for Central American products under the CBI, he said.
